faq.question: How is a case manager different from a legal assistant?
faq.answer: A legal assistant supports attorneys day-to-day with admin tasks. A case manager **owns the case itself** — they're responsible for driving it forward, coordinating all parties, and making sure nothing stalls between open and close. They think proactively, not reactively.

faq.question: How many cases can one case manager handle?
faq.answer: It depends on case complexity and stage. A full-time case manager typically handles **30–60 active cases** comfortably in a PI environment. We set expectations during the consultation call based on your specific caseload.

faq.question: How do they get access to case information?
faq.answer: Your case manager works directly in your case management system — Clio, Filevine, MyCase, or whatever you use. You **grant them access with appropriate permissions**, and they operate within your existing setup. No new tools, no parallel systems.

faq.question: Is there a contract or minimum commitment?
faq.answer: We have a service agreement but **no long-term lock-in**. You can exit at any time with no penalties. Our results are what keeps clients with us — not the fine print.

faq.question: What if they're not the right fit?
faq.answer: Tell us and we'll **rematch you at no extra cost**. A case manager needs to fit your firm's communication style and expectations — and finding that fit is part of what we guarantee.
